body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Election Day, and the biggest local story is the final stretch of the CA-22 congressional race, where a new poll puts Democrat Randy Villegas ahead of Republican incumbent David Valadao. Outside, expect a mild November day — a high near 71, a low around 53 tonight, moderate air quality, and no active weather alerts or fires in Kern County.

## The Kern Overnight

Kern County dispatch logged 25 incidents between 7:05 p.m. and 5:00 a.m., a busy night led by nine fire calls, eight medical and overdose responses, six disturbances and welfare checks, and two suspicious-person reports.

The evening opened quietly enough, with medical aid calls on Lexington Avenue and Pioneer Drive before 8 p.m. and a suspicious-person report shortly after 7. Fires were reported at 7:42 p.m., 8:16 p.m., and again at 10:03, 10:25, and 11:26 p.m., the last of those on Woodrow Avenue. Welfare checks came in on East Brundage Lane and elsewhere through the late evening, and deputies logged a domestic call just before 11:30 p.m.

The overnight hours stayed active. A welfare check on Center Street came in at 12:39 a.m., followed by medical aid on South Chester Avenue at 1:13 a.m. and a fire at 1:44 a.m. Fires were also reported on Bagwell Court at 2:12 a.m. and at 2:38 and 2:58 a.m., with welfare checks on East Beardsley Avenue and Alberta Street in between. The log closed with medical aid calls at 4:08 and 5:00 a.m., the last on East Brundage Lane. All of these remain preliminary dispatch reports until an official source confirms them.

## Today's weather

It's 54 degrees at Meadows Field this morning, on the way to a high near 71 and a low around 53 tonight — a classic early-November Bakersfield day, mild and dry. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and no active fires are being tracked. Air quality sits at 72, which registers as moderate; if you're sensitive to particulates, it's worth keeping an eye on as the day warms. Otherwise, it's a good day to be outside, and a good day to get to a ballot drop-off if you haven't yet.

## Top stories

**Bakersfield Now reports that the Kern County Sheriff's Office is asking for the public's help identifying a suspect in a burglary at Faith Temple Church.** Deputies are seeking tips as they work to identify the person believed responsible. If you have information, contact the Sheriff's Office directly rather than approaching anyone on your own.

**According to 23ABC, a final poll in the 22nd Congressional District shows Democrat Randy Villegas leading Republican incumbent David Valadao 52% to 41% among 356 likely voters.** The survey, sponsored by the USC Center for the Political Future and conducted by the USC Democracy and Fair Elections Lab, carries a margin of error of 5.2 points. When undecided voters were pushed to choose, Valadao gained ground, narrowing the result to 54-44 — still within that margin. Voters surveyed named cost of living as their top issue at 19%, followed by immigration or ICE at 12% and the economy or business at 10%. USC political science professor Christian Grose noted that about one in five Latino voters and a contingent of 2024 Trump voters said they intend to back Villegas.

**23ABC also spent time at Bakersfield College talking with voters about what's drawing them to the polls — and what isn't.** As of Friday, about 19% of eligible Kern County voters had cast ballots, and county election officials project turnout between 40% and 50%, which they describe as high for a midterm. Public health professor Charles Daramola pointed to the economy and high prices, while student Deema Ebeid said these elections shape the future of her generation. One student, Elijah, said he doesn't plan to vote and finds the volume of voter information overwhelming; the elections office offers voter information guides for exactly that reason. Voting ends today — mail-in ballots must be postmarked by Nov. 3, there are 20 drop-off locations across the county, and in-person polls close at 8 p.m.

**KGET 17 reports that the seventh movement of the city's $1.5 billion freeway interchange project is now complete, with the three-year construction of the final leg set to begin in 2027.** It's a milestone years in the making, and it moves the project closer to full completion.

**23ABC reports that one woman is dead and two others were injured after a shooter opened fire into a crowd leaving a large Halloween gathering on Rosedale Highway early Sunday morning.** The Kern County Sheriff's Office says deputies were dispatched to Rosedale Highway near Gibson Street just after 12:30 a.m. for reports of an armed robbery in progress and arrived to find three women with gunshot wounds as several hundred people were leaving the area. One woman died at the scene; the other two were hospitalized with injuries described as non-life-threatening. A surviving victim told 23ABC she heard a group of about three men discussing what sounded like a robbery before the shooting, and that the shooter had reportedly been turned away from the venue earlier. The Sheriff's Office said the investigation is still in its early stages.

**KGET 17 reports that six people were killed over the Halloween weekend across the area** — a sobering tally that underscores how heavy the past few days have been for first responders and families.

**And KGET 17 shares that Christopher Russell is proud of his "Christmas Prayer Tradition,"** a local effort that has become a meaningful part of the season for those who take part.

## Something good

There's real satisfaction in watching a project that has shaped daily commutes for years finally click into place. The seventh movement of the city's $1.5 billion freeway interchange is complete, and while the final leg doesn't start until 2027, every finished piece means smoother merges and shorter backups for the thousands of us who use those ramps. It's the kind of progress you feel in your commute before you ever read about it.

## Coming up this week

Election Day tops the calendar today, with in-person polls closing at 8 p.m. and mail ballots needing a Nov. 3 postmark. If you still have a ballot on the kitchen counter, the county's 20 drop-off locations are the fastest route.

On the civic side, the Police Civil Service Commission meets Wednesday, Nov. 4, at 8:30 a.m., and the City Council has two sessions that same day — Meeting 330 at 3:30 p.m. and Meeting 515 at 5:15 p.m. The Planning Commission follows on Thursday, Nov. 5, at 5:30 p.m. Agendas are posted ahead of each meeting if you want to look before you go.

For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a full slate. Journey USA takes the stage Saturday, Nov. 7, alongside TEXAS TORNADO TRADITION that same evening. The 2026 Golden Empire Youth Cheer EXPO fills the Fox on Sunday, Nov. 8, and Cults & Classics: Play Misty for Me screens Monday, Nov. 9. Looking further out, NUTCRACKER! Magical Christmas Ballet arrives Nov. 13, and season passes for the 2026-2027 Cults & Classics series are already on sale.

Have a good Tuesday, and if you're voting, thank you for taking the time.
